title: Krishnamoorthi Says Stamp Out Hate After Seattle Diwali Disruption
excerpt: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi condemned the targeting of Seattle's Diwali celebration in a post on X, joining Rep. Pramila Jayapal and community groups in calling the anti-Hindu placards hateful and racist.
body:
• Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi on Sunday condemned the disruption of Seattle's Diwali celebration, saying in a post on X: "we have to stamp out this hate directed toward Hindus and anyone."
  • The new statement adds a second Indian American member of Congress to the response, after Rep. Pramila Jayapal called the display "vile and racist" — Krishnamoorthi thanked Jayapal for highlighting it.
  • Far-right activists Jake Lang and Thomas Allen entered the Seattle Center Armory on Saturday carrying placards reading "Deport All Dot Heads" and "Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians" while children were performing, according to CoHNA.
  • For readers celebrating Diwali in the Seattle area: CoHNA has advised community members to stay vigilant, saying the activists announced plans to disrupt other celebrations.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi has condemned the disruption of a Diwali celebration in Seattle, becoming the latest Indian American lawmaker to speak out after far-right activists targeted the festival with anti-Hindu placards. In a post on X on Sunday, Krishnamoorthi said Diwali is supposed to celebrate the victory of light over darkness, but added that "that victory is not automatic."

"Today is Diwali… Happy Diwali to everyone celebrating today," he wrote, according to ANI. Referring to the slogans at the Seattle event, he added: "When people are chanting 'Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians' and other hateful anti-Indian and anti-Hindu slogans, you know we have a lot of work to do."

"Let's proudly light a lamp today for Diwali, but resolve that we have to stamp out this hate directed toward Hindus and anyone."

— Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, in a post on X

We covered the disruption itself earlier today in our report on the Seattle Diwali celebration disrupted by protesters carrying 'Deport All Dot Heads' placards. Krishnamoorthi's statement is a new development in that story: it widens the congressional response beyond Seattle's own representative and frames the incident as part of a broader pattern of anti-Hindu and anti-Indian rhetoric in the United States.

What happened in Seattle

The incident took place on Saturday at the Seattle Center Armory, where the Diwali: Lights of India programme was being held as part of Seattle Center Festál. According to Zee News, Jake Lang and Thomas Allen appeared near the stage carrying American flags and placards bearing the messages "Deport All Dot Heads" and "Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians" while a cultural performance was under way. Attendees confronted the protesters, who were subsequently escorted out.

The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said children were performing when the men arrived. In its community alert, reported by ANI via Indian Economic Observer, CoHNA said others at the venue "didn't tolerate this and removed them from the premises," and advised community members to stay vigilant while celebrating Diwali, as the activists had announced plans to disrupt other celebrations.

The response so far

Krishnamoorthi thanked Rep. Pramila Jayapal for highlighting the incident. Jayapal, who represents Seattle in the US House of Representatives, had said on X: "I am beyond disgusted by this vile and racist display. Diwali is an important holiday and our community should feel safe to celebrate it. This hateful display has no place in our city or this country."

Indian-American businessman and former White House adviser Ajay Jain Bhutoria also criticised the demonstration, calling it "pure hate and bigotry" and saying targeting Hindu Americans and Indian immigrants with racial slurs has no place in the country, according to Zee News.

Lang, for his part, posted on X after the confrontation alleging that he and other protesters had been assaulted by attendees, and blamed Hindus for electoral outcomes in Texas. ANI reported that Lang runs an organisation called White Replacement, took part in the January 6, 2021 attack on the US Capitol, served four years in jail, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump on the first day of his second presidency in 2025.

Why it matters for the diaspora

For Hindu American and Indian American families, Diwali celebrations in public venues such as the Seattle Center Armory are community events — with children's performances, music and family activities — not political rallies. The practical takeaway from CoHNA's alert is vigilance, not withdrawal: organisers and attendees in the Seattle area have been advised to watch for further announced disruptions during the Diwali period and to alert venue staff or law enforcement if protesters attempt to enter an event.

What happens next

No further official action was reported in the sources on Sunday. What to watch is whether other lawmakers join Krishnamoorthi and Jayapal, and whether Seattle-area Diwali events over the coming days proceed without further disruption. Krishnamoorthi's closing line set the tone he wants the community to take from the day: light a lamp, and resolve to stamp out the hate.
